what: A 256-bit AVX-VNNI inner for the K-quant prefill owner. The owner's fast inner was gated on avx512f+avx512bw+avx512vnni, so every consumer Intel part from 12th gen onward -- which has AVX-VNNI on 256-bit registers but no AVX-512 at all -- fell back to the plain AVX2 inner. This adds a ymm-width twin of the existing zmm kernel and dispatches to it only when the 512-bit gate is false.
lever: q4_k_owner_weight_row_block_avxvnni, selected when the K-quant owner is on AND avx512vnni is absent AND avxvnni+avx2 are present. Additive: the AVX-512 path, the repack8 path, and the scalar path are byte-identical to main.
camelid_head: a047ab8c3 (branch perf/kquant-avxvnni-inner, on top of upstream/main 3a95e4c93)

host.cpu: win i9-14900HX 8P+16E (24 physical / 32 logical), Raptor Lake
host.isa: avx2=true fma=true avxvnni=true; avx512f=false avx512bw=false avx512vnni=false
host.why_this_host_matters: It is the exact shape the old gate misses: VNNI dot-product instructions present, AVX-512 absent. On this class of part the owner was permanently on its slowest vector inner.
host.gpu: RTX 4060 Laptop present but hidden with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 for every measurement; unhidden, the GPU silently takes prefill and the CPU inner is not what is being timed.

method.harness: camelid bench-owner-sweep --lane kquant --max-tokens 1 (prefill only; decode is not on this lever)
method.pairing: all three arms run once per round inside one process, interleaved, so a per-round ratio cancels thermal and clock drift. 2 warmup rounds discarded.
method.why_pairing_is_required: absolute throughput slid ~11% over a long run on this host (the 'off' arm drifted 46.9 -> 41.7 tok/s) while the per-round ratio held flat at ~1.13. An unpaired A-then-B comparison on this laptop measures the cooling, not the kernel.
method.statistic: median of per-round ratios, 95% percentile bootstrap CI over rounds (2000 resamples)
method.engagement_check: every row carries owner_prefill_taken and kquant_avxvnni256_taken. A non-off arm with a zero counter is a fake null and is discarded, not reported.

results.baseline_for_ratios: owner_avx2 (the arm this change replaces). The 'off' column is included only to show the owner itself is still the larger lever.

p606_8_rounds_repeat.note: independent repeat of the row above, run on a different day-part; the CIs overlap

results.shape: the win tapers with prompt length -- widest at ~124 tokens, narrowest at 2421. The honest claim is +11-13%, not a single headline number.
results.owner_vs_off: 1.7691x at 606 tokens. The owner is still worth more than this inner; this receipt does not promote it.

engagement_accounting.note: This is the strongest structural evidence in the receipt, because it reproduces exactly across two unrelated architectures.
engagement_accounting.counter_scopes: The two counters are deliberately scoped differently, which is what makes the difference between them readable: kquant_owner_prefill_taken increments in BOTH q4_k_block_dot_core_with_repack and q6_k_block_dot_core (all K-quant owner matmuls), while kquant_avxvnni256_taken increments only in q4_k_owner_prefill_tiled (the Q4_K tiled path). Their difference is therefore the Q6_K matmul count, not an unexplained shortfall.
engagement_accounting.scaling: counters scale exactly with chunk count: llama 606 tok = 3 chunks -> 588/504, 2421 tok = 10 chunks -> 1960/1680
engagement_accounting.reading: 6 of every 7 owner matmuls per layer take the new inner. The 7th is the Q6_K tensor that Q4_K_M mixes in per layer; it routes to q6_k_owner_prefill_tiled, which has NO VNNI path on any host. So the measured +11-13% is a diluted number -- roughly a seventh of the owner's matmul work never sees VNNI at all.
engagement_accounting.vnni512_taken: 0 in every arm on this host, confirming the 512-bit path is genuinely unreachable here and the two kernels are not both firing.

parity.unit: q4_k_owner_avxvnni_inner_is_bit_identical asserts kquant_owner_avxvnni_taken > 0 BEFORE comparing, so it cannot pass vacuously, then compares to_bits() against q4_k_block_dot_core. It also asserts kquant_owner_vnni_taken == 0. It runs 8 input rows against ROW_BLOCK = 64, so the path it covers is the PARTIAL row-block tail; full 64-row blocks are covered by the sweep and e2e runs, where a chunk is hundreds of rows.
parity.instruction_level: _mm256_dpbusd_avx_epi32 was separately checked against a scalar reference over the operand range the kernel actually feeds it.
parity.why_it_must_be_exact: VNNI accumulates the same u8 x i8 products into the same i32 lanes as the AVX2 sequence; the reduction order inside a 32-value block is unchanged, so there is no reassociation to lose.

blast_radius.avx512_hosts: provably unaffected -- the new branch requires !use_vnni, so any host that selects the 512-bit inner never evaluates it.
blast_radius.non_avxvnni_hosts: unaffected -- falls through to the same use_avx2 branch as before.
blast_radius.default_state: the K-quant prefill owner itself remains env_flag_default_off (src/runtime_config.rs:80). This change makes the owner faster when it is switched on; it does not switch anything on.

negative_controls: Running with CUDA visible collapses the difference because the GPU takes prefill (4.6s vs 26s) -- every number here was taken with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1.

An earlier '~15% over AVX2' figure from a single round at 1.1 GiB free RAM was RETRACTED; it did not survive paired repetition. The memory-pressure explanation offered for it was also retracted after the counters showed zero file reads.
A leaked CAMELID_WIN_HYBRID_POLICY=off from a previously failed run made two arms measure the same thread width. The harness now clears every knob at the start of each arm.
test_suite_state: Full lib suite shows 3 failures. 2 reproduce on clean upstream/main (the pre-existing pair documented in #558). The 3rd passes in isolation on this branch and fails only under full-suite parallelism. None are in the K-quant path.
verdict: Lands as an additive fast path: +11-13% prefill over the AVX2 inner whenever the K-quant owner is enabled on a VNNI-without-AVX-512 host, 44/44 paired rounds across two model architectures and four prompt lengths, bit-identical output, and no reachable change on any other host.
open_questions: q6_k_owner_prefill_tiled has no VNNI path on ANY host, 512-bit or 256-bit. That is a seventh of the owner's per-layer matmuls in a Q4_K_M mix and is the obvious next lever; it is not addressed here.

The Q8 owner gates on the same avx512f+bw+vnni triple (inference.rs:16880) and is ALREADY default-on. So every Q8 model on 12th-gen-and-later consumer Intel is running its AVX2 inner today. Same gap, wider blast radius, unmeasured here.
One host. AVX-VNNI is also present on Alder/Meteor/Arrow Lake and on Zen 5; the ratio on a part with a different cache hierarchy or without a P/E split is unmeasured.
Q4_K only. Other K-quant widths in the owner were not swept.
The taper with prompt length is reproducible but unexplained -- most likely the inner stops being the bottleneck as chunk count grows, but that was not instrumented.
